html:
Tanganyika Territory was the British-ruled mainland of what is now Tanzania, held under a League of Nations mandate from 1922 and a United Nations trusteeship after 1946, until independence on 9 December 1961.

Britain ruled through chiefs and spent little. Its biggest scheme, the groundnut scheme, failed. Because it was a trust territory, the United Nations sent missions and heard petitions, which helped the nationalists.

The Tanganyika African National Union, founded in 1954 by Julius Nyerere, won all the elected seats and led the country to independence without violence. Tanganyika joined with Zanzibar after the revolution of 1964.
sum: Tanganyika Territory was the British-ruled mainland of what is now Tanzania, held under a League of Nations mandate from 1922 and a United Nations trusteeship after 1946, until independence on 9 December 1961.
